content.user_title: Debug CUDA Crashes with FlashInfer Logging
content.value_statement: CUDA crashes often hide the inputs and state that caused the failure. This skill uses FlashInfer logging and NVIDIA tools to expose actionable diagnostic evidence.
actual_capabilities: Configures FlashInfer API logging levels and destinations for crash reproduction.
Explains how to inspect tensor shapes, dtypes, devices, strides, contiguity, and statistics.
Maps common CUDA failures to focused checks in the captured API log.
Separates logs by process for multi-GPU and distributed debugging.
Combines API logging with compute-sanitizer and cuda-gdb workflows.
Shows selective kernel printf, assertions, and synchronization for lower-level diagnosis.
limitations: Only FlashInfer APIs decorated with @flashinfer_api produce API logs.
Requires access to a reproducible CUDA workload and the relevant NVIDIA debugging tools.
Logging identifies suspicious inputs but does not prove the root cause or repair code automatically.
Level 5 statistics are skipped during CUDA graph capture.

use_cases.title: Diagnose inference crashes
use_cases.description: Inspect a failing inference workload and compare tensor shapes, dtypes, devices, and statistics before the crash.

use_cases.title: Isolate a failing rank
use_cases.description: Separate logs by process to identify the first failing rank in a distributed FlashInfer workload.

use_cases.title: Trace kernel memory faults
use_cases.description: Combine API logs with compute-sanitizer, cuda-gdb, and kernel printf output to isolate illegal memory writes.

prompt_templates.title: Enable basic crash logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to enable FlashInfer API logging at level 3 for my_script.py and save output to crash_log.txt. Explain what each setting captures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a first CUDA crash investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an illegal memory access
prompt_templates.prompt: My FlashInfer run reports an illegal memory access. Help me inspect the final logged API call for shape, dtype, device, stride, and contiguity problems.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review captured tensor metadata for a common CUDA failure.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a multi-GPU failure
prompt_templates.prompt: My eight-rank job fails on one GPU. Design a logging plan using per-process destinations, then explain how to compare successful and failed ranks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Identify the failing process in a distributed workload.

prompt_templates.title: Build a kernel-level investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a debugging sequence for a persistent CUDA memory fault. Combine FlashInfer level 3 logs, compute-sanitizer, cuda-gdb, and selective kernel printf checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Escalate from API evidence to kernel-level debugging.

output_examples.input: The final API call has query head dimension 128 and cache head dimension 64.
output: Likely cause: the kernel received incompatible head dimensions.
Next check: confirm the API contract, rebuild the cache with dimension 128, and rerun with level 3 logging.

output_examples.input: Level 5 logging reports 128 NaN values and no infinite values in the input tensor.
output: Likely cause: an earlier operation introduced invalid numerical values.
Next check: inspect the preceding successful API call for extreme values, division by zero, or uninitialized data.

output_examples.input: A distributed run fails, but only one per-process log ends without an API output record.
output_examples.output: Focus on that rank's final input record, then compare its shapes, device, and dtype against a successful rank.

best_practices: Start with level 3 logging to capture useful metadata without expensive tensor statistics.
Write crash logs to a protected file so output survives process termination.
Reproduce with the smallest failing workload before adding sanitizer or kernel-level instrumentation.
anti_patterns: Do not leave detailed logging enabled in production workloads.
Do not assume the last successful API call caused the failure; inspect the first call without output.
Do not use kernel printf from every thread because output volume can hide the relevant signal.

faq.question: Does this skill execute debugging commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic instructions and example commands; you decide what to run in your CUDA environment.

faq.question: Which logging level should I use first?
faq.answer: Start with level 3 for shapes, dtypes, devices, and metadata. Use level 5 only when investigating NaN or Inf values.

faq.question: Can the logs contain sensitive information?
faq.answer: Yes. Protect logs before sharing because they can reveal tensor metadata, process details, file paths, and software versions.

faq.question: Why are statistics missing during CUDA graph capture?
faq.answer: FlashInfer skips level 5 statistics during graph capture to avoid synchronization that could invalidate the capture.

faq.question: Will every FlashInfer API produce logs?
faq.answer: No. Only APIs using the @flashinfer_api decorator produce these records, and decorator coverage may be incomplete.

faq.question: Which external tools does the tutorial cover?
faq.answer: It covers compute-sanitizer for memory checks, cuda-gdb for stack inspection, and selective kernel printf output.
